facts.statement: Neuquensuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliform that lived during the Santonian age of the Upper Cretaceous in Neuquén Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Neuquensuchus (meaning "Neuquén crocodile", referring to the city) is an extinct genus of crocodyliform from the Santonian-age Upper Cretaceous Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Neuquén Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The fossils of Neuquensuchus were discovered on the campus of the Universidad Nacional del Comahue in the city of Neuquén.
facts.quote: The known remains were discovered on the campus of Universidad Nacional del Comahue in the city of Neuquén.

facts.statement: Neuquensuchus was named by Lucas E. Fiorelli and Jorge O. Calvo in 2007, with the publication becoming available in 2008.
facts.quote: Neuquensuchus was named by Lucas E. Fiorelli and Jorge O. Calvo in a publication dated to 2007, but which became available in 2008.

facts.statement: Neuquensuchus had a shin longer than its thigh, a trait suggesting it possessed some running ability unlike most other crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Unlike the great majority of crocodyliforms, its shin was longer than its thigh, suggesting it had some running ability.

facts.statement: Neuquensuchus was a small animal with upper arm bones measuring about 10.0 centimeters, a thigh bone about 9.4 centimeters, and a shin bone about 10.5 centimeters long.
facts.quote: It was not a large animal; the upper arm bones of the type specimen measure about 10.0 centimeters (about 3.9 in) long, the thigh bone about 9.4 centimeters (about 3.7 in) long, and the shin bone about 10.5 centimeters (about 4.1 in) long.

facts.statement: Neuquensuchus had a shin longer than its femur, a condition shared only with Shantungosuchus among known crocodyliforms with measurable leg bones.
facts.quote: Unlike all known crocodyliforms with measurable leg bones except Shantungosuchus, the shin was longer than the femur.

facts.statement: While later analyses placed Neuquensuchus in the notosuchian clade Ziphosuchia, an analysis by Gabriel Liu and colleagues in 2017 upheld its original classification.
facts.quote: While several subsequent cladistic analyses recovered Neuquensuchus as a member of the notosuchian clade Ziphosuchia, a position which is more consistent with the fossil record and paleobiogeography of non-neosuchian mesoeucrocodylians, the original position was upheld by an analysis conducted by Gabriel Liu and colleagues in 2017.

facts.statement: Neuquensuchus was likely a swift, land-living animal with limb proportions well-suited for running.
facts.quote: Neuquensuchus, a small, slender crocodyliform, had limb proportions well-suited to running, and was probably a swift, land-living animal.

facts.statement: Neuquensuchus lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)
